questions.question: Which language was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act** was enacted in **2003** to include four additional languages in the **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The four languages added through this amendment were **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali**.
 
• **Bodo** is a language primarily spoken in the **Bodoland Territorial Region** of **Assam** and belongs to the Tibeto-Burman language family.
 
• **Maithili** is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly in the **Mithila region** of **Bihar** and parts of **Jharkhand**.
 
• **Santhali** is the most widely spoken Munda language, used by the **Santhal tribal community** residing in **Jharkhand**, **Odisha**, **West Bengal**, and **Bihar**.
 
• Following the inclusion of these four languages, the total count of recognized languages in the **Eighth Schedule** increased from **18** to **22**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Eighth Schedule** originally consisted of **14** languages at the time of the Constitution's commencement.

 
 
• The **21st Amendment Act, 1967** introduced **Sindhi** as the 15th language.
 
• The **71st Amendment Act, 1992** added three more languages: **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, and **Nepali**.
 
• **Dogri**, the fourth language added in 2003 along with Bodo, Maithili, and Santhali, is spoken primarily in the **Jammu and Kashmir** region.
 
 
 
• Constitutional provisions related to official languages are found in **Part XVII**, covering **Articles 343 to 351**.
 
 
• **Article 344(1)** provides for the constitution of a Commission by the **President of India** to make recommendations regarding the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes.
 
• **Article 351** provides a directive for the development and promotion of the **Hindi language** as a medium of expression for the composite culture of India.

questions.question: During which occasions is Giddha commonly performed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weddings and harvest festivals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular and vibrant folk dance originating from the **Punjab** region of India and Pakistan, specifically performed by **women**.
 
• The dance is a hallmark of joyous occasions and is most commonly performed during the **harvest season**, particularly during the festival of **Baisakhi**, which marks the Punjabi New Year and the reaping of **Rabi crops**.
 
• It is an essential part of **Punjabi weddings**, where female relatives and friends gather to celebrate the union through rhythmic movements and playful singing.
 
• The performance is characterized by the singing of **Boliyan** (short traditional couplets) that express a wide range of emotions, from humor and teasing to domestic life and social commentary.
 
• Unlike formal classical dances, **Giddha** is a social activity that takes place during **Teeyan** (the monsoon festival) and other family celebrations like the birth of a child.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance Characteristics**:

 
 
• **Style and Form**: It is often considered the feminine counterpart to **Bhangra**. While Bhangra is high-intensity and athletic, Giddha focuses on grace, elegance, and rhythmic **clapping** (Taali).
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**: The primary rhythm is created by the dancers’ hands, but it is often supported by a **Dholak** (a two-headed hand drum) played by an elder woman or a professional musician.
 
• **Attire**: Dancers wear bright-colored **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** paired with heavily embroidered **Phulkari** dupattas. Key traditional ornaments include the **Sagghi Phul** (hair ornament) and heavy necklaces.
 
• **Cultural Significance**: It serves as a medium for women to express their creative energy and share their lived experiences in a patriarchal society through the medium of **storytelling** and dance.

questions.question: Who determined the value of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Cavendish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant**, represented by the symbol **G**, is a fundamental physical constant that appears in **Sir Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation**.
 
• **Henry Cavendish**, an English physicist and chemist, successfully determined the value of **G** through a series of experiments conducted between **1797 and 1798**, known as the **Cavendish experiment**.
 
• The primary objective of his experiment was to measure the **density of the Earth**, but the results provided the first accurate calculation of the gravitational constant.
 
• Cavendish utilized a **torsion balance**, which featured a horizontal wooden rod suspended by a thin wire with small **lead spheres** at each end; he measured the tiny gravitational attraction between these and larger stationary lead masses.
 
• By observing the **deflection** of the rod and the **twisting** of the suspension wire, he quantified the force of gravity, leading to the derivation of **G**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton**:

 
 
• Formulated the **Inverse Square Law** of gravitation in his work **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
 
• While he identified the relationship **F = G × m₁m₂ / r²**, he did not possess the experimental means to measure the value of **G**.
 
 
 
• **Johannes Kepler**:
 
 
• Famous for his **three laws of planetary motion** which described the orbits of planets as ellipses.
 
• His work was purely **kinematic** and did not include the gravitational constant or the physical cause of planetary motion.
 
 
 
• **Albert Einstein**:
 
 
• Proposed the **General Theory of Relativity** in **1915**, redefining gravity as the **curvature of spacetime** rather than a standard force.
 
 
 
• The value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ N m² kg−²**.

questions.question: In tennis, what does a score of "deuce" mean?

options.text: The game is tied, but not at 40-40.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The score is tied at 40-40.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Tennis**, the term **Deuce** describes a specific situation in a game where both the server and the receiver have won three points each, resulting in a score of **40-40**.
 
• The traditional scoring progression in a tennis game follows the sequence of **Love** (0 points), **15** (1 point), **30** (2 points), and **40** (3 points). When both sides reach 40, the score is called **Deuce** rather than 40-all.
 
• Once a game reaches deuce, a player must win **two consecutive points** to win the game. The first point won after deuce gives that player the **Advantage**, and the second consecutive point secures the game.
 
• If the player with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to **Deuce**. This cycle continues until one player wins two points in a row from a deuce state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scoring Terminology**:

 
 
• **Love**: Refers to a score of **zero**. It is widely believed to have originated from the **French** word **l'oeuf** (meaning egg), which symbolizes the shape of a zero.
 
• **Advantage In (Ad-in)**: This is the score when the **Server** wins the first point after a deuce.
 
• **Advantage Out (Ad-out)**: This occurs when the **Receiver** wins the first point following a deuce.
 
 
 
• **Etymology and Rules**:
 
 
• The word **Deuce** is derived from the **French** word **deux**, meaning two, or the phrase **à deux de jeu**, signifying that the players are two points away from winning the game.
 
• In some modern formats, such as **Professional Doubles** or certain amateur leagues, **No-Ad (No Advantage)** scoring is used. In this system, a **deciding point** is played at deuce, and the winner of that single point wins the entire game immediately.

• This rule is only applicable when the defending team has at least **6 or 7 players** active on the mat; if the number of defenders drops to 5 or fewer, the bonus point rule becomes **inactive**.

• **Point System and Revivals**:

• A **Touch Point** is scored when the raider tags one or more defenders and returns safely to their own half of the court.

• The project was modeled after the **Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)** of the **United States**, focusing on the unified development of a river basin spanning **West Bengal** and **Jharkhand** (formerly part of Bihar).
 
• The primary objectives of the corporation include **flood control**, **irrigation**, **water supply** for domestic and industrial use, and **soil conservation**.
 
• DVC operates a network of major dams including **Tilaiya**, **Konar**, **Maithon**, and **Panchet**, which regulate the flow of the **Damodar River** and its tributaries like the **Barakar River**.
 
• The corporation is a major producer of **electricity**, utilizing both **hydro-electric** and **thermal power** stations to fuel the industrial growth of the **Chhota Nagpur plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steel Production**:

 
 
• While the DVC area encompasses the **Steel Hub of India** (including **Bokaro** and **Durgapur**), the corporation itself provides the **power and water infrastructure** rather than engaging in the manufacturing process of steel.
 
 
 
• **Trade Promotion**:
 
 
• This refers to activities intended to stimulate the **exchange of goods**. Although DVC supports the economy, it is a **resource management** agency and not a trade-facilitating body.
 
 
 
• **Rural Credit**:
 
 
• This involves providing **financial loans** to the agricultural sector, which is the specialized function of institutions like **NABARD** and **Regional Rural Banks**, not a river valley corporation.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact**:
 
 
• Beyond its engineering goals, DVC is responsible for **afforestation**, **malaria control**, and the **socio-economic well-being** of the inhabitants living within the **Damodar Valley**.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) scheme is designed for which group?

• The **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM)** is a **Central Sector Scheme** launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** in **February 2019** to provide old-age protection and social security.
 
• The scheme is specifically designed for **Unorganized Sector Workers**, a demographic that constitutes nearly **93 percent** of India total workforce and often lacks formal pension support.
 
• To be eligible, an applicant must fall within the **entry age of 18 to 40 years**, ensuring a consistent contribution period before reaching retirement.
 
• The scheme targets low-wage earners with a **monthly income of 15,000 rupees or less**, focusing on those most vulnerable to economic instability in their later years.
 
• Under this initiative, subscribers receive a **minimum assured monthly pension of 3,000 rupees** once they attain the age of **60 years**.
 
• The financial structure is based on a **50:50 matching contribution**, where the **Central Government** contributes an amount equal to the monthly premium paid by the beneficiary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Beneficiaries include **street vendors**, **mid-day meal workers**, **head loaders**, **brick kiln workers**, **cobblers**, **rag pickers**, **domestic workers**, and **agricultural laborers**.
 
• It also encompasses **handloom workers**, **leather workers**, and those engaged in similar informal occupations.
 
 
 
• **Exclusion Criteria**:
 
 
• Workers already covered under organized social security frameworks like the **Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO)**, **Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)**, or the **National Pension System (NPS)** are ineligible.
 
• Individuals who fall under the **income taxpayer** bracket are also excluded from the benefits of the PM-SYM scheme.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Framework**:

• Enrollment is conducted through **Common Service Centres (CSCs)** using an **Aadhar card** and a **Savings Bank Account** or **Jan Dhan account** with **IFSC**.
 
• In the event of the subscriber death, the **spouse** is entitled to receive **50 percent** of the pension as a family pension, provided the spouse is not already a beneficiary.

questions.question: According to the new policy for central government-run schools, what support is offered to students who fail their annual exams in Classes 5 and 8?

• Under the revised guidelines, students in **Class 5** and **Class 8** are required to appear for **regular annual examinations** at the end of each academic year to assess their learning progress.
 
• If a student fails to secure the minimum passing marks in these annual exams, the school is legally obligated to provide **additional instructions** or **remedial coaching** specifically targeted at the subjects the student failed.
 
• Following the period of **additional coaching**, the student must be granted a **re-examination opportunity** within a period of **two months** from the date of the original result declaration.
 
• The primary objective of this provision is to ensure that the student is not immediately detained and is given a fair chance to bridge **learning gaps** and demonstrate proficiency before a final decision on detention is made.

• The **2019 Amendment** was introduced to address concerns regarding falling **educational standards** and the lack of accountability in the learning process.
 
• It gives the **appropriate government** (Central or State) the power to decide whether to continue the no-detention policy or allow schools to detain students who fail the re-examination.
 
• The **National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)** provides the framework for these assessments to ensure they align with defined **Learning Outcomes** for each grade level.

Standard Algebraic Identities

Square of sum: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and Square of difference: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Comparison of Surds

If a + b√x = c + d√x (where a, b, c, d are rational), then the rational parts must be equal (a = c) and the irrational coefficients must be equal (b = d).

Squaring Surds

The square of a term like (x√y) is calculated as x² × (√y)² = x² × y.

questions.question: There are two numbers such that the first number is half of the second number. If their average is 72, then what is the first number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the **first number** to the **second number** is 1 : 2.

Sum of the two numbers = **Average** × 2 = 72 × 2 = 144.

Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 = 3 parts.

3 parts = 144 ⇒ 1 part = 144 ÷ 3 = 48.

The **first number** (representing 1 part) is 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average** of two numbers = 72

**First number** = 1/2 × **Second number**

**Formula Used:**

**Average** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d714acc8dfdefb7d6a0b44f424151a2a88d4019e8f40fa539fab3ba400084a7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **second number** be 2x.

⇒ The **first number** = (1 ÷ 2) × 2x = x.

⇒ **Average** = (x + 2x) ÷ 2

⇒ 72 = 3x ÷ 2

⇒ 144 = 3x

⇒ x = 144 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 48

The **first number** is x = 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The **average** of a set of numbers is the sum of the numbers divided by the count. Formula: **Average** = Σx ÷ n.

Ratio Distribution

To find a specific part from a total sum given a ratio a : b, use the formula: Part A = [a ÷ (a + b)] × **Total Sum**.

Relationship between Mean and Sum

The **total sum** of observations can always be found by multiplying the **average** by the number of observations (Sum = **Average** × n).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average** of this Arithmetic series = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 = (53 + 289) ÷ 2 = 171.

**Number of terms (n)** = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Difference] + 1 = [(289 − 53) ÷ 2] + 1 = 119.

**Total Sum** = Average × Number of terms = 171 × 119 = 20349.

**∴ The correct answer is 20349.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 53

Last term (l) = 289

Common difference (d) = 55 − 53 = 2

**Formula Used:**

Number of terms (n): l = a + (n − 1)d

Sum of n terms (Sₙ): Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3650646fda0ce874b457114aa0a4aeb8d357abff339450d7e6eee1a051e7657a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 289 = 53 + (n − 1) × 2

⇒ 289 − 53 = (n − 1) × 2

⇒ 236 = (n − 1) × 2

⇒ n − 1 = 236 ÷ 2 = 118

⇒ n = 118 + 1 = 119

⇒ S₁₁₉ = (119 ÷ 2) × (53 + 289)

⇒ S₁₁₉ = (119 ÷ 2) × 342

⇒ S₁₁₉ = 119 × 171

⇒ S₁₁₉ = 20349

**∴ The correct answer is 20349.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of first n natural numbers

The sum is calculated using the formula: S = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Sum of first n odd numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is always n².

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence where each term is obtained by adding a fixed **common difference (d)** to the preceding term.

questions.question: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 34 cm. Area of this rhombus is 120 square cm. What is the side (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of **diagonals** d₁ × d₂ = 2 × **Area** = 2 × 120 = 240.

Given sum d₁ + d₂ = 34. Two numbers with sum 34 and product 240 are 24 and 10.

The **half-diagonals** of the rhombus are 12 cm and 5 cm (24/2 and 10/2).

Applying the **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13), the **side** of the rhombus is 13 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of diagonals (d₁ + d₂) = 34 cm

Area of rhombus = 120 cm²

**Formula Used:**

1. Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

2. Side (a) = √((d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²) or 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3865f02051c4f64ff2810ef3eeeff07086b5bcb87d0003ede10f1dfc45b6d380.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = 120

⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 240

⇒ We know that (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2 × d₁d₂

⇒ 34² = d₁² + d₂² + 2 × 240

⇒ 1156 = d₁² + d₂² + 480

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 1156 − 480 = 676

⇒ Since 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

⇒ 4a² = 676

⇒ a² = 676 ÷ 4 = 169

⇒ a = √169 = 13 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

All **four sides** are equal and **opposite angles** are equal. The **diagonals** bisect each other at **90°**.

Side-Diagonal Relation

The side 'a' and diagonals d₁, d₂ are related by **4a² = d₁² + d₂²**, which is derived from the **Pythagoras theorem** in one of the four internal triangles.

Perimeter of Rhombus

The **perimeter** of a rhombus is calculated as **4 × side**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factor out 4: 4 × (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 111)

Number of terms (n) = 444 ÷ 4 = 111

Sum of **n natural numbers** = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2

Total Sum = 4 × [111 × 112 ÷ 2] = 2 × 111 × 112 = 24864

**∴ The correct answer is 24864.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Series: 4, 8, 12, ..., 444

This is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** where:

First term (a) = 4

Common difference (d) = 8 − 4 = 4

Last term (l) = 444

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aecf776725aae2dda51aa5c166cb8662d6980f104ce786765377e12dab708a59.png] 

**Formula Used:**

nth term of AP (l) = a + (n − 1)d

Sum of n terms (Sₙ) = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 444 = 4 + (n − 1) × 4

⇒ 444 − 4 = (n − 1) × 4

⇒ 440 = (n − 1) × 4

⇒ n − 1 = 440 ÷ 4

⇒ n − 1 = 110

⇒ n = 111

Now, calculate the sum:

⇒ Sₙ = (111 ÷ 2) × (4 + 444)

⇒ Sₙ = (111 ÷ 2) × 448

⇒ Sₙ = 111 × 224

⇒ Sₙ = 24864

**∴ The correct answer is 24864.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula Sₙ = [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Arithmetic Progression Properties

The **average** of terms in an AP is always equal to (First term + Last term) ÷ 2. The total sum is then Average × Number of terms.

Number of Terms in AP

The number of terms (n) in an AP can be quickly calculated as n = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1.

questions.question: There are total 20 hats of blue and red colour. The average cost of blue colour hats is Rs. 50. The average cost of red colour hats is Rs. 35. The average cost of all the hats is Rs. 44. What is the number of red colour hats?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By **Alligation Method**, the ratio of **Blue hats** to **Red hats** is:

(Average of all − Red Average) : (Blue Average − Average of all)

⇒ (44 − 35) : (50 − 44) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2

Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5 units. Given 5 units = 20 hats, so 1 unit = 4 hats.

Number of **Red hats** = 2 units × 4 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total hats = 20, Average cost of **Blue hats** = Rs. 50, Average cost of **Red hats** = Rs. 35, Combined average cost = Rs. 44.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/178b26ae82f23a66d9e086d50d05848185ae6cd289bd6ac49a03c040c412ca75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of **Red hats** be R.

⇒ Then the number of **Blue hats** = 20 − R.

⇒ Total Cost = (Number of Blue × Avg Blue) + (Number of Red × Avg Red)

⇒ Total Cost = 20 × 44 = 880.

⇒ 50 × (20 − R) + 35 × R = 880

⇒ 1000 − 50R + 35R = 880

⇒ 1000 − 15R = 880

⇒ 15R = 1000 − 880 = 120

⇒ R = 120 ÷ 15 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is calculated as A = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and a is the individual average.

Alligation Rule

It states that the ratio of the quantities is inversely proportional to the difference of their averages from the mean average: (Quantity 1) ÷ (Quantity 2) = (Average 2 − Mean Average) ÷ (Mean Average − Average 1).

Ratio Separation

To find a specific component value from a ratio x : y, use the formula: Value = [x ÷ (x + y)] × Total Quantity.

questions.question: What is the Highest Common Factor of 5/12, 15/20 and 25/30?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **HCF of fractions**, use the formula: **HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators)**.

Numerators: 5, 15, 25 ⇒ **HCF** = 5.

Denominators: 12, 20, 30 ⇒ **LCM** = 60.

Required HCF = 5/60 = 1/12.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Fractions 5/12, 15/20, and 25/30.

**Formula Used:** **HCF of Fractions** = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d9357ce75ab75560fa3dfae6a6ad29d36bf8fc3ab28008a9abb1ddece7d789f.png] 

⇒ First, simplify fractions to their lowest terms:

⇒ 5/12 (Already simplified)

⇒ 15/20 = (15 ÷ 5) / (20 ÷ 5) = 3/4

⇒ 25/30 = (25 ÷ 5) / (30 ÷ 5) = 5/6

⇒ New set of fractions: 5/12, 3/4, 5/6

⇒ HCF of Numerators (5, 3, 5) = 1

⇒ LCM of Denominators (12, 4, 6) = 12

⇒ Resulting HCF = 1/12

**∴ The correct answer is 1/12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Fractions

To find the Least Common Multiple of fractions, use the formula: LCM = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators).

Simplest Form Requirement

Always convert fractions to their simplest (lowest) form before applying the HCF or LCM formulas to avoid incorrect results.

HCF Definition

The **Highest Common Factor** is the largest possible number that divides each of the given numbers exactly without leaving any remainder.

questions.question: What is the least number, which when divided by 8, 14, 15 and 20 leaves remainder 5 in each case?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required least number = **LCM**(8, 14, 15, 20) + **Common Remainder**

LCM of (8, 14, 15, 20) = 840

Required number = 840 + 5 = 845

**∴ The correct answer is 845.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Divisors** = 8, 14, 15, 20

**Common Remainder** (r) = 5

**Formula Used:**

Least number = **LCM**(Divisors) + r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a2716df58b41f5ca863ae8be31d91ca763d22ad705f92bcc9e0b34700af423a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of divisors:

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 14 = 2 × 7

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ **LCM** = Highest power of all prime factors = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ **LCM** = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840

⇒ Required number = 840 + 5

⇒ Required number = 845

**∴ The correct answer is 845.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Concept

When a number leaves the same remainder 'r' when divided by several numbers, it is always in the form: (LCM × k) + r, where k = 1, 2, 3...

Different Remainder Case

If divisors are a, b, c and remainders are x, y, z such that (a−x) = (b−y) = (c−z) = k, then the least number = LCM(a, b, c) − k.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

questions.question: A person paid Rs. 18 as tax on an article worth Rs. 200. What is the rate of tax?

Identify the **Base Value** and the **Tax Amount**.

Use the direct percentage formula: (Part ÷ Whole) × 100.

Worth of the Article = ₹200

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e246a71701108ad899ed6d416ddb677e4c0c3718ce67f4be06b39fd9b2d2b12.png] 

**Calculations:**

Direct Percentage Formula

The basic formula for percentage is: **Percentage** = (Value ÷ Total Value) × 100. This is used for tax rates, profit margins, and discount rates.

Reverse Calculation of Worth

If the **Tax Rate** and **Tax Amount** are known, the original value can be found using: Worth = (Tax Amount × 100) ÷ Tax Rate.

Effective Tax on Total Price

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 800. Loss percentage is 25 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = 25% = 1/4 (where 1 is **Loss** and 4 is **CP**).

Given: Loss (difference) = 1 unit = Rs. 800.

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

SP = 3 × 800 = Rs. 2400.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference (CP − SP) = Rs. 800

Loss Percentage = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Cost Price (CP) − Selling Price (SP)

Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9b602b3774db16fbe2b2e9e8fe3ade76d218cf7e9147818fe9abe960f332645.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = 25% of CP

⇒ 800 = (25 ÷ 100) × CP

⇒ CP = 800 × 4

⇒ **CP** = Rs. 3200

⇒ SP = CP − Loss

⇒ SP = 3200 − 800

⇒ **SP** = Rs. 2400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit occurs when **Selling Price (SP)** is greater than **Cost Price (CP)**, while Loss occurs when CP is greater than SP.

Calculation Base

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated using the **Cost Price (CP)** as the denominator.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100. In this case: SP = 3200 × (100 − 25) ÷ 100 = 3200 × 0.75 = Rs. 2400.

questions.question: There are 100 men in a group. They have food for 90 days. After 30 days, 100 more men join the group. Remaining food will last for how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **remaining food** after 30 days is sufficient for the initial **100 men** for **60 days** (90 − 30).

When **100 more men** join, the total number of men **doubles** (from 100 to 200).

In inverse proportion, when the number of men **doubles**, the **time** it lasts is **halved**.

Required days = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**<

questions.question: The speed of A and B is 25 km/hr and 10 m/s respectively. What is the respective ratio of the distance covered by them in one hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Speed of B** from m/s to km/hr: 10 × (18 ÷ 5) = **36 km/hr**.

Since **Time** is the same (1 hr), the **Ratio of Distances** is equal to the **Ratio of Speeds**.

Required Ratio (A : B) = 25 : 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Speed of A** = 25 km/hr, **Speed of B** = 10 m/s, **Time** = 1 hr.

**Formula Used:** **Distance = Speed × Time**; To convert speed from m/s to km/hr, multiply by **18/5**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de21ad409ddc842edebffa0a25d327198525df05fd947a60bcf2b79b7997aa0a.png] 

⇒ **Speed of A** = 25 km/hr

⇒ **Speed of B** (in km/hr) = 10 × (18 ÷ 5) = 2 × 18 = **36 km/hr**

⇒ **Distance covered by A** in 1 hr = 25 × 1 = 25 km

⇒ **Distance covered by B** in 1 hr = 36 × 1 = 36 km

⇒ Required **Ratio** = 25 : 36

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance-Speed Relation

When **Time** is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed: D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed = **Total Distance Covered ÷ Total Time Taken**.

questions.question: A train moving with the speed of 90 km/hr crosses a platform in 12 minutes. Length of the train and the platform is same. What is the length (in metres) of the platform?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed in m/s = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s.

Time in seconds = 12 × 60 = 720 s.

Total Distance (Train + Platform) = Speed × Time = 25 × 720 = 18000 m.

Since lengths are same, Platform Length = 18000 ÷ 2 = 9000 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 9000 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**
